title: Verify a new anonymous user can complete the entire preference questionnaire with valid data
description: This test verifies the primary happy path for a first-time anonymous user, ensuring they can fill out all fields in the guided questionnaire and receive personalized job matches. This workflow is critical for demonstrating immediate value and driving user engagement.
testDescription: As a new job seeker visiting the platform for the first time, I want to complete the guided questionnaire with all my preferences so that the system can provide me with a highly relevant, personalized set of job listings without requiring me to sign up first.
prerequisites: User is a new visitor with no existing session cookies for the platform. The home page is accessible and the questionnaire feature is enabled. The backend job matching service is available.
stepsToPerform:
1. Open a new incognito/private browser window to ensure an anonymous session.
2. Navigate to the application's home page. Observe that the guided questionnaire is presented.
3. For 'working arrangement', select the 'Fully Remote' option.
4. For 'motivation', select 'Income'.
5. In the 'annual salary' field, enter the numeric value '120000'.
6. For 'location', select 'United States'.
7. For 'job titles', enter 'Senior QA Lead'.
8. For 'years of relevant experience', enter the numeric value '10'.
9. For 'highest level of education', select 'Master's Degree'.
10. For 'most valued workplace benefit', select '401(k) Matching'.
11. Click the 'See My Matches' or equivalent submission button.
expectedResult:
1. The questionnaire is submitted successfully without any validation errors.
2. The user is redirected to a personalized job results page.
3. The job listings displayed are filtered and ranked based on all the preferences provided (e.g., remote roles, salary near $120k, QA titles).
4. The user's preferences are successfully stored and associated with their anonymous session.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Collect the seeker's requirements through a short guided questionnaire offered from the home page on a first visit, before any account exists.

title: Verify the system correctly records which preferences were provided and which were left unanswered when a user submits a partial questionnaire
description: This test ensures the system can gracefully handle partially completed questionnaires, a common user behavior. It verifies that provided data is used for matching and that the system correctly tracks the state of unanswered fields.
testDescription: As a new job seeker, I may not want to answer every question. I want to provide only my most critical preferences (like job title and work arrangement), submit the form, and still receive relevant job matches, with the system remembering which questions I skipped.
prerequisites: User is a new, anonymous visitor. The questionnaire is designed to allow submission with optional fields left blank. A method to inspect session data (e.g., browser developer tools) is available for verification.
stepsToPerform:
1. Open a new incognito/private browser window and navigate to the home page.
2. Start the guided questionnaire.
3. For 'job titles', enter 'Marketing Coordinator'.
4. For 'working arrangement', select 'Hybrid'.
5. For 'years of relevant experience', enter '2'.
6. Deliberately leave the 'annual salary' field blank.
7. Deliberately leave the 'highest level of education' field unselected.
8. Click the 'See My Matches' or equivalent submission button.
9. After redirection, inspect the anonymous session data stored by the application.
expectedResult:
1. The partial questionnaire is submitted successfully.
2. The user is redirected to a job results page based on the provided preferences (Marketing Coordinator, Hybrid, 2 years experience).
3. Inspection of the session data confirms that values for 'job titles', 'working arrangement', and 'experience' are stored.
4. The session data explicitly shows that 'annual salary' and 'education' were left unanswered (e.g., their corresponding keys are null or absent).

sourceCitation.excerpt: Record which preferences were provided and which were left unanswered.

title: Verify the system rejects a resume upload that is just over the defined size limit with a clear reason
description: This test verifies that the system correctly enforces the maximum file size limit for resume uploads, providing clear feedback to the user when a file is too large. This is crucial for managing system resources and ensuring a good user experience. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: As a job seeker, when I try to upload a resume file that exceeds the platform's specified size limit, I expect the system to prevent the upload and inform me clearly about the size restriction so I can correct the issue. This test uses a file size of 5.1MB against a 5MB limit.
prerequisites: The maximum resume file size is defined in the system configuration as 5MB. A test file that is slightly larger than the limit (5.1MB) is available. The user is an anonymous visitor with no existing session.

2. Start the guided questionnaire for job preferences.
3. Proceed through the questionnaire to the 'Resume Handling' section.

7. Observe the system's response to the upload attempt.

expectedResult:

2. A user-friendly error message is displayed, clearly stating that the file exceeds the maximum allowed size (e.g., 'File size exceeds the 5MB limit. Please upload a smaller file.').
3. The oversized file is not retained by the system or associated with the user's session.
